answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Domain registrar history with renewals changes that arithmetic: a domain renewed five years running, so the plume for each fake is paid in the real world. Scale stops helping the attacker here. Ten clones need ten separate proofs, each with its own a domain renewed five years running, and the canyon grows linearly while the reward per clone stays flat. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the umber of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
